clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: Immediately after using a hollow-bore needle for client care, an RN sustains a needlestick that breaks the skin. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Wash the puncture site with soap and water, report the exposure promptly, and obtain immediate occupational-health evaluation.
options.B: Squeeze the puncture until it bleeds freely, clean the site with bleach, and wait for the source client's test results before reporting.
options.C: Cover the puncture with a bandage, finish the medication pass, and report the exposure at the end of the shift if symptoms develop.
options.D: Apply alcohol hand rub to the puncture, document the event in the client chart, and arrange employee-health follow-up for the next day.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC/NIOSH guidance for healthcare workers with occupational blood exposure instructs the worker to wash needlestick or sharps punctures with soap and water, report the incident promptly, and immediately seek medical evaluation to determine exposure risk and the need for post-exposure management. OSHA likewise directs workers who sustain a needlestick to clean the wound immediately, report the exposure immediately to the employer, and seek immediate medical attention; OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens requirements make confidential post-exposure medical evaluation and follow-up available promptly after an exposure incident. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan places biohazard handling and staff/workplace safety within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. A therefore gives the correct immediate sequence. B uses inappropriate wound manipulation/bleach and delays reporting. C postpones evaluation until the end of the shift and conditions reporting on symptoms, which defeats time-sensitive exposure management. D substitutes alcohol hand rub for recommended wound washing, places occupational-exposure documentation in the wrong record context, and delays evaluation. Therefore A is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: After a percutaneous occupational blood exposure, immediately wash the site with soap and water, report the exposure promptly through the facility process, and obtain immediate medical/occupational-health evaluation rather than delaying care or using caustic wound treatments.

Rebuilt the item around immediate occupational needlestick management using current CDC/NIOSH, OSHA and NCSBN guidance. Removed the prior correct-answer length cue.

scope_exclusions.specific_PEP_regimen: Not tested; post-exposure prophylaxis depends on the exposure/source evaluation and current occupational-health guidance.
scope_exclusions.source_client_testing_process: Not tested; the RN should report and obtain evaluation promptly without waiting for source testing to be completed.
scope_exclusions.employee_exposure_documentation_in_clien: Not endorsed; occupational-exposure reporting follows the facility's employee/exposure process and applicable confidentiality requirements.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0623 tests acute workplace-violence security response. V2-Q0622 tests malfunctioning-equipment removal/reporting. V2-Q0274 tests medication-error event reporting. V2-Q0626 tests immediate personal first aid plus occupational-health reporting/evaluation after a percutaneous blood exposure. Targeted repository search for needlestick/sharps-exposure content returned no matching item before staging.

option_audit.A: Correct. It follows the current CDC/NIOSH and OSHA sequence of immediate washing, prompt reporting and immediate evaluation.
option_audit.B: Plausible attempt to reduce inoculum but uses inappropriate wound manipulation/bleach and delays the required reporting/evaluation process.
option_audit.C: Plausible workflow-continuation response but improperly delays time-sensitive occupational exposure management and ties reporting to symptoms.
option_audit.D: Plausible decontamination/reporting response but substitutes alcohol hand rub for soap-and-water wound care and delays evaluation until the next day.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. CDC/NIOSH and OSHA agree on immediate wound cleansing, prompt reporting and immediate medical evaluation. A alone contains all three. B/C/D each delay or distort essential components of the response.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. Correct option A is the shortest, not the longest, and the choices remain structurally parallel action sequences.
